setting: The galaxy is alive and crowded — dozens of minor living alien species trading, scheming, and feuding across a busy frontier. No empire, no tomb, no single mind: a marketplace. Black-market curios move hand to hand, and an artifact's power is inseparable from its provenance — half of which is forged. Everyone wants a cut of one contested commodity that is not what the brokers say it is; tracing it to its real source is the deal nobody dares close. The spine is mercantile noir: whose history is real, who you deal with, who you cross — and the relic's true chain of custody, lies stripped oldest to newest, down to a singular true origin.

civs.name: the-vossan-syndics
civs.trait: consortium of merchant-clans who set prices, launder provenance, and fence the best forgeries

civs.name: the-khariti-drift
civs.trait: tramp-fleet caravans who carry curios between ports and remember which papers are fake

civs.name: the-oseni-assayers
civs.trait: neutral appraisers who certify provenance for a fee — bribable, but the only ones who can read a true chain

civs.name: the-melun-cartel
civs.trait: ruthless runners who corner the contested commodity and salt the market with counterfeits

civs.name: the-rho-collectors
civs.trait: obsessive private buyers who pay anything for a relic with a clean story, real or not

climax_label: the true origin behind the forgeries
